description: Given a list of integers arr sorted in non-decreasing order and an integer elem, return the index of the last occurrence of elem in arr, or -1 if elem does not occur. A non-negative result must be a valid index whose element equals elem, with no later element equal to elem; a result of -1 means that no element equals elem. The input list is not modified.
notes: VERINA reads the output index with Lean's arr[i]!, which yields 0 for an out-of-range index. Both specs instead require a non-negative result to be a valid index (result < length), so they reject only the degenerate outputs that VERINA accepts through that default value (an out-of-range index when the searched value is 0, where the empty suffix makes VERINA's condition hold). As in VERINA, negative results other than -1 are not constrained.
